script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for October 7. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

A glass jar can hold leftovers, store tools, become a vase, and organize supplies before ever needing recycling.  Reuse gets more life from what already exists—more value per resource, less waste per use.

Manufacturing costs are sunk—already spent. But value remains until the item fails completely. Discarding before full use wastes the investment. Reuse captures remaining value. Reuse isn't just using things the same way—it's finding new purposes.  A ladder becomes a bookshelf.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: The value in things persists.  Getting more use from what exists is often better than making something new.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Reuse Inventory - What Still Has Value?.

Here's your activity: What do you own that still has value but you're not using? Old skills, unused equipment, dormant relationships? How could you extract more value from what you already have before acquiring something new? This helps you identify reuse opportunities in possessions and experiences.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about using things again can be applied to reuse inventory - what still has value?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
